title: SDK micro-instrumentation phase and latency-binning infra
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We currently rely on coarse-grained timers emitted from the edge proxies and service mesh to drive latency dashboards. Those timers miss short critical spans (SDK/handler-level hot paths) and create noisy tail-percentile signals. Goal: introduce a lightweight, opt-in SDK micro-instrumentation layer that emits high-precision latency buckets for request lifecycle phases (client serialization, outbound network, token generation, model-forwarding, streaming flush). The data will feed the metrics/log pipeline and a new latency-binning dashboard so we can (1) explain tail latency sources, (2) correlate with error spikes, and (3) power adaptive routing decisions.
technical_design: Design decisions: 1) Implement a minimal C API surface for native SDKs (Go/Python/Node) to record phase timestamps with constant-space overhead (ring counters) and an optional coarse sampling rate. 2) Emit two event types: phase-timer events (fast, no stack), and summarized bucket events (periodic flush). 3) Use delta-encoded millisecond deltas and a tiny header to avoid inflating request payloads. 4) Default behavior: disabled for free-tier; enabled for Dedicated/Private by config and behind a runtime feature-flag. 5) Backwards compatibility: SDKs must degrade to no-op when server doesn't accept micro-instrumentation headers.
implementation_notes: - SDK helper: Instrument.startPhase(name) / Instrument.endPhase(name) lightweight handle. Internals use monotonic clock and pre-allocated per-request scratch buffer. - Binning strategy: fixed bins [0-1ms,1-4ms,4-16ms,16-64ms,64-256ms,256-1024ms,>1024ms] chosen from production histogram sweep. - Flush policy: per-request inline header when size <= 512 bytes; otherwise aggregate into 1s background flush to telemetry collector. - Transport: send as compressed event to /v1/telemetry/events or attach to request envelope header X-RW-MINSTR (base64 gzip). - Metrics mapping: phase_timer.bucket.<phase>.<bin> -> counter; phase_timer.sampled.<phase> -> gauge sample rate. - Add sampler hints: SDK exposes setSamplingHint(rate, key) for downstream agents to honor.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Risk: extra bytes on hot request paths; mitigated by strict size threshold and default off for free-tier. - Tradeoff: per-request inline flush gives best fidelity but higher CPU and bandwidth. We choose inline for requests under 256B micro-instr payload, background otherwise. - Privacy: micro-instrumentation does not include user payloads; only numeric deltas and phase names. Security review flagged (done) and no PII expected. - Stability: server-side parsing added to ingestion but will be feature-flagged; if ingestion becomes a bottleneck we will roll to aggregated-only mode.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs (Go/Node/Python) implement API and pass micro-benchmark: <1% p50 CPU overhead at 1000 RPS per core. 2) Telemetry pipeline ingests new event type and emits metrics with <5s end-to-end latency for inline flush. 3) New latency-binning dashboard available in Console; can break down tail sources by phase with top-5 phase contributors. 4) Integration test simulates bursty traffic (2x baseline) and shows no pipeline OOM or spike in per-tenant egress >10%. 5) Feature flag exists and toggles behavior without client SDK upgrade.
rollout_plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal tenants and infra team; collect perf and storage metrics for 72h. - Phase 2 (beta): open to Dedicated customers via Console toggle; increase sampling to 10% for beta. - Phase 3 (general availability): default enabled for Dedicated/Private with conservative sampling and cost recommendations. - Rollback: feature toggle off and clear instrumentation headers at edge.
test_plan: - Microbench harness in gomicrobench repo: measure CPU/memory per request at 10k/s synthetic. - End-to-end staging test: replay traffic with instrumentation headers and validate counters appear in pipeline and dashboard. - Fault injection: drop telemetry collector to ensure SDK degrades to no-op and doesn't block request path. - Security: static review of header encoding and audit KMS usage for any persisted payloads.
